answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard work-set requirement, ensuring an honest node pays 80 watts while 1,000 fakes incur a delta of overhead, stalling their access. A verifier challenges agents with a random pattern, a sable-toned map of memory-latency checks, to reject shared-cache entities. Any kernel error or inconsistent latency trigger results in a permanent ban, assuming distinct memory buses are mandatory. Each extra identity adds significant operational costs to the vault of memory, and non-compliant agents forfeit all assets to the network.
